chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

When one swears three consecutive oaths truthfully, he has quarrelled and upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal); and when one swears with one false oath, he has quarrelled and upon him is blood.

key_terms.أَيْمَانٍ مُتَتَابِعَاتٍ: Consecutive oaths, referring to multiple oaths sworn in succession.
key_terms.جَادَلَ: To quarrel or dispute, here used as a technical term for a specific legal consequence of swearing.
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood, referring to the slaughter of a sacrificial animal as a penalty or expiation.

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for swearing three consecutive oaths truthfully or one oath falsely in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific conditions under which an oath incurs the penalty of 'dam' (sacrificial animal) within the context of Ihram, emphasizing that both three consecutive truthful oaths and a single false oath constitute 'jadal' (quarreling/arguing). Scholarly tradition interprets 'dam' here as the expiation for breaking the oath, linking the verbal act of swearing directly to ritual obligations. This ruling highlights the severity of verbal commitments in Shia jurisprudence, where even truthful repeated oaths can trigger legal consequences if they lead to dispute.
